executive_conclusion: The evidence suggests that the UTC-weekday daily-range distributions differ, with an omnibus epsilon-squared of 0.0186. The practical and temporal stability is reflected in a conservative MODERATE evidence rating; the result is descriptive and not a trading strategy.

hypotheses.alternative: At least one weekday has a different daily high-low range distribution.
hypotheses.null: The distribution of EUR/USD daily high-low range is identical across Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday under the preregistered daily and eligibility definitions.

limitations: Raw timestamp open-versus-close convention is unresolved.
Daily observations may be serially dependent and volatility-clustered.
UTC calendar days are descriptive and are not local trading sessions.
Task 02 coverage categories do not establish market-calendar causes.
Complete-day filtering can alter the represented date population.
Sensitivity-only profiles are diagnostic populations, not substitutes for the primary population.
Range behaviour does not establish direction, profitability, or a trading rule.
observed_fact: The primary Kruskal-Wallis comparison returned p=1.34975e-16 across 4,127 complete UTC weekday dates. The registered weekday median order was Thursday|Friday|Wednesday|Tuesday|Monday.
registration_classification: correctively registered replication of the developed Task 04 analysis
registration_disclosure: The study design was locked before the corrected production regeneration. However, the underlying analysis had already been developed and its results reviewed. The corrected production run is therefore treated as a registered replication of the development analysis, not as a pristine first-look preregistration.

registry.registration_classification: correctively registered replication of the developed Task 04 analysis
registry.title: Daily Range Behaviour by Weekday

robustness.chronological: The final 30% validation period had p=0.00216501 and weekday-order rank correlation 0.700 with the full sample.
robustness.coverage_profiles: STRICT_CONTINUITY remained significant with rank correlation 0.90 against the primary ordering. The diagnostic SENSITIVITY_FULL and SENSITIVITY_2023 populations contained 398 and 16 complete dates and were not significant; their ordering was not concordant with the primary population.
robustness.extreme_events: The raw primary result remains authoritative. The 1st/99th winsorised and largest-1%-excluded comparisons retained the same weekday median ordering, with p-values 1.339e-16 and 2.091e-15; both transformations are reversible sensitivity checks only.
robustness.volatility_regime: 3,947 dates received LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH labels from strictly past-only information; warm-up dates remain unclassified. Omnibus p-values were 6.315e-16 (LOW), 0.001135 (MEDIUM), and 0.411 (HIGH). The registered analysis did not detect a statistically significant weekday difference in the HIGH-volatility subset. This non-significant result does not establish equivalence or absence of a weekday effect.
robustness.yearly: 17 calendar years met the preregistered per-weekday sample threshold; 9 had an unadjusted yearly omnibus p-value below 0.05. All years remain in the outputs, and ordering was not uniform.
